High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:131917
Court No. - 68
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 26823 of 2024

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
Learned A.G.A. has informed that the notice to the informant has been served on 11.07.2024.
2. Heard Sri Chandra Bhushan Prasad, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.184 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. read with Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Shahganj, District Agra, during the pendency of trial.

PROSECUTION STORY:
4. The applicant is stated to have enticed away the minor sister of the informant aged about 17 years on 08.04.2024 at about 11:00 a.m. when she had gone to fetch her mark-sheet from the school.
The victim is stated to have taken away Rs.40,000/- and all her papers alongwith her from the house.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
5. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
6. The FIR is delayed by about two days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

7. The victim is a consenting party as is evident from the fact that she had taken away Rs.40,000/-
from the house.
Although she has stated that the applicant had rendered her unconscious in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
She has further stated that she stayed with the applicant at Delhi for 17 days.
She has also stated that she was taken to the police station by the parents of the applicant.
8. As per high school certificate, the date of birth of the victim is stated to be 14.10.2006, as such she is only six months less than 18 years.
By her physical appearance, she seems to be major.
9. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
10. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 27.04.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE BY A.G.A./INFORMANT:
11.
The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

CONCLUSION:
12. The Supreme Court in Sushil Kumar vs. Rakesh Kumar, (2003) 8 SCC 673 has stated that it is more often in the Indian Society that person shows the age of their wards much below than their actual age.

entities.text: Sushil Kumar vs. Rakesh Kumar, (2003) 8 SCC 673
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also settled by Supreme Court that as per the medical records, a leverage of two years may be granted to the accused person.

In the case of Brij Mohan Singh vs. Priya Brat Narain Sinha, AIR 1965 SC 282, this Court, inter alia, observed that in actual life it often happens that persons give false age of the boy at the time of his admission to a school so that later in life he would have an advantage when seeking public service for which a minimum age for eligibility is often prescribed.

entities.text: Brij Mohan Singh vs. Priya Brat Narain Sinha, AIR 1965 SC 282
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

14. ?A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is Sameer vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51615707/
2 established beyond a reasonable doubt.

entities.text: Sameer vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
15.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ?Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
16. ?Learned A.G.A. could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
17. ?It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned A.G.A.
18.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant- Sameer involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
20. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

21. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
